Although many North American utilities are still piloting EVMC, Baltimore Gas and Electric’s recently expanded EVMC program forecasts costs of around $50/vehicle-year for incremental participation in 2026–2027, excluding customer participation incentives for a DLC- like implementation with 20,000–30,000 participating vehicles (Michel 2024). This suggests a range of costs of tens of dollars per vehicle-year may be policy-relevant as EVMC programs are scaled up beyond the pilot level. Whether price-responsive EVMC can achieve savings similar to those seen in this study under perfect-foresight is contingent on how well real-life forecasting approximates perfect-foresight. Contemporary power system operator experience and forecast quality suggest high-quality forecasting is feasible. Best-practice load forecasting and machine learning methods exhibit around 1% normalized mean average error in hour-ahead and 2%–4% normalized mean average error in day-ahead load forecasts (Bryce et al. 2023). EV loads are still small in North American jurisdictions compared to future EV adoption projections, but if similar forecasting errors can be achieved for price-responsive EV loads, implemented results should be closer to perfect- foresight than to no-foresight. Also, although the quantitative savings per vehicle-year results of this study are particular to the system studied and all of our modeling assumptions, we would expect our high-level findings to hold qualitatively for all bulk power systems. That is, well- forecast TOU responses based on individual vehicles charging at power levels moderated to use more of the dwell period than minimum-time charging can provide significant savings up to moderate shares of the LDV fleet. This study made several key assumptions that could be relaxed in future work. Setting the baseline charging profile assuming ubiquitous charging with vehicles immediately plugging in after every trip results in an unrealistically high number of plug-ins per vehicle and per week (Smart and Salisbury 2015). This also likely enhances the contrast seen in this study between within-session and within-week charging flexibility. On the other side of the ledger, assuming charging can be managed any time the vehicle is parked overstates the within-week flexibility resource, which is also impacted by the assumption that all vehicles start and end the week with a full SOC. In focusing on bulk power system LDV EVMC production cost savings, this work does not estimate other potential EVMC savings or EVMC enablement costs. Regarding savings, we do not investigate EVMC’s potential to displace long-term power generation investments or EVMC’s ability to reduce distribution system costs, both of which can provide significant additional savings highly dependent on system particulars but likely to be in the range of tens to hundreds of dollars per vehicle-year (Anwar et al. 2022).
